description:
The IKEA Effect — explained in 60 seconds.

You overvalue anything you helped build — furniture, software, ideas, teams.

What actually happens in your brain: Labor creates attachment. Your effort gets woven into the object's worth, inflating it far beyond market value.

Try it today: Want people to care about the project? Let them build a part of it. Ownership is manufactured by effort.

narration: 99% of people get this completely backwards.
You probably believe this: THINGS HAVE FIXED VALUE. But that's not the full story.

You overvalue anything you helped build, furniture, software, ideas, teams. Here's what's happening: Labor creates attachment. Your effort gets woven into the object's worth, inflating it far beyond market value.
Norton, Mochon & Ariely in 2012, people's willingness to pay for self-assembled IKEA items rose sharply versus identical pre-built ones.
Want people to care about the project? Let them build a part of it. Ownership is manufactured by effort. That's your Mindforge move for today. Follow for tomorrow's.
